expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "No. Your test cannot fail." and "A check that would have stayed green throughout the entire incident isn't a device — it's a rumour."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "the pipeline can lose its join key and still publish a plausible number, because `COALESCE(x, 0)` converts 'this row didn't match' into 'this customer earned nothing.'"

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconcile warehouse revenue total against the source/billing system, within tolerance"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: "Build to staging → assert → promote" and "makes all the above able to *stop* publication rather than email about it"

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Schema contract at ingest: assert the expected column set; a rename hard-fails the load"

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Volume/total assertion vs. same weekday historically (floor and ceiling)" and "Assert unmatched-row count = 0 after the join"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: "Why nothing caught it for three weeks: the only reconciliation in your system is the finance close. Your detection latency is exactly one month by construction."

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: No explicit comparison between silent wrong and failed pipeline. Discusses the hazard and detection gap but not the danger differential.
